claim: stability and sensitivity evidence for the edge resolver: not a proof of soundness
fixture_model: synthetic function/instruction/call-index fixtures fed to the production evidence pass and edge-record builder; no real object file or linker is exercised
non_claims: A PASS is not a soundness result: the corpus shows that named transformations do not change the named properties, not that no transformation can.

A monotone residual bound is not a completeness result: the fixpoint cannot admit a function that no materialised-address evidence names, and the closure cases use synthetic evidence, not a real image.
The neutral-rebuild case is a metamorphic relation on the identity function.  Byte-identical .text across independent real builds is a separate measurement, not something this fixture establishes.

The identity cases bind the enumerated analysis inputs (sections, relocations, symbol tables, loader entries).  They do not prove that no other input exists, and the fixtures are not real ELF section tables.
The fixtures are synthetic and do not reproduce the real library's layout, linker behaviour, or runtime dispatch.
The refusal cases establish that the named disagreements are detected; they do not establish that every real derivation is complete.

The validator compares a record's own ledgers (target_set, admitted_targets, provenance chain) and the final upper-bound oracle.  The ledgers are mutually redundant within the record, not independent derivations.  It does not re-derive the target set to a fixpoint, so a record that is internally consistent and consistent with the upper bound is not thereby proved complete, and it cannot distinguish an analyzer-produced record from a forged one that is internally consistent.  Admissibility needs the identity chain (tool sha256, artefact sha256, sidecar digest) and a re-run of the pinned validator over the pinned sidecar.
not_covered: real linker behaviour at scale (section GC, identical-code folding, symbol versioning)
PLT/GOT tricks beyond the fixture's link-time constant thunk slot
provider dispatch tables selected at runtime
admission by refutation of a *real* excluded writer/caller; the corpus exercises the caller-bound shape on a synthetic bound, not a real image
the full library's real instruction idioms; the fixtures use the instruction shapes the semantic rule recognises
